Today I came to Mumbai and it reminded me of this hospital. In 2024 I admitted my sister here but forgot to write the review. So here it is.

It was early morning and my sister had sudden pain in her stomach. Looking at the pain I was quite evident that it was due to stone. As we were near to Parakh hospital we reached there. As per doctor's advice ultrasound was done and as I thought it was due to stone only. We requested doctor to provide some medicine for getting relief from pain so that we can go back to Gwalior and we will take further treatment there as it is our hometown. But he insisted for getting admitted. Considering the pain we decided for getting admitted. They kept giving my sister injections and medicines for holding the pain. Also ran some other tests. After 24 hours they started insisting for surgery. We finally decided to get discharged from the hospital. The total expense that we had to pay for this 1 day was 30000/-
Worse part was that immediately after the discharge the pain returned and my sister was still in the same situation as 1 day before.
At last I went to a medical store nearby and told him about the pain. The medical store guy gave just 1 pill and with that medicine the entire pain vanished and my sister reached back Gwalior via train without any pain.
In Gwalior she took homeopathy medicine treatment and in six months all the stones are gone without any surgery.

So I'm not sure about how this hospital is at present but in October 2024 they literally looted us in just a single day. So beware.

Did you know your family history could hold important clues about your breast and ovarian cancer risk? 

BRCA is a gene that helps repair damaged cells and maintain normal cell growth. Changes (mutations) in BRCA genes can increase the risk of developing breast and ovarian cancers, making early risk assessment important. 

Who should consider a BRCA assessment? 
• Individuals with a family history of breast, ovarian, or related cancers 
• Breast cancer patients, especially those diagnosed at a younger age 
• Ovarian cancer patients 
• Individuals with multiple family members affected by cancer 
• Anyone concerned about inherited cancer risk 

You may benefit from a genetic consultation if: 
• You are a breast cancer survivor and BRCA positive and want to understand the risk for your children or siblings. 
• A close family member had BRCA-positive breast or ovarian cancer. 
• Your grandmother or parent was BRCA positive and you wish to know when to get assessed. 
• Multiple women in your family have had breast or ovarian cancer. 
• Cancer runs in your family, even if you have no symptoms. 
• You were diagnosed with breast cancer at a younger age. 
• You have already undergone genetic testing and would like expert guidance on your results. 
If any of these situations apply to you, visit your nearest M|O|C Cancer Care for a FREE Genetic Consultation with our expert oncologists from 27th May 2026 to 15th June 2026.

featured_reviews.name: Bijal Domadia
featured_reviews.review_text:
IN COTINUATION WITH YOUR LAST REVIEW REPLY You mentioned the following arguments in your defence.  THOUGH NON OF THE POINT IS RELEVANT DURING OUR VISITS. IT BECOMES DIFFICULT FOR THE SENIOR CITIZENS ALSO TO SIT FOR A LONGER DURATION . MY LAST VISIT TOOK ALMOST 3 HOURS WAITING TIME.
Usually the reasons for a delay are as follows:
- patients earlier in the appointment list not coming on time.... THAT DOES NOT MEAN THE LATER PATIENTS HAS TO SUFFER WHO COME ON TIME. ELSE TAKING APPOINTMENT IS A WASTE POLICY.
- patients in pain taking longer for curative procedures / cleanups. THAT IS VERY RARE AND NOT EVERYTIME
Children especially are often uncooperative & tend to go beyond allotted appointment. MOSTLY WHENEVER ME OR MY FAMILY VISITED SENIOR CITIZENZ WERE THERE. ALL CHILDREN DONT TAKE LONG TIME.
- patients with more serious complaints or requiring surgery need more detailed explanations. ALL PATIENTS EXPECT DETAIL INVESTIGATION AND EXPLANATIONS
-(rarely) patients in unbearable pain or bleeding may be taken out of turn, thereby hampering the appointments. BETTER STOP TAKING APPOINTMENT AND TAKE FIRST COME FIRST SERVE BASIS
Since every patient requires a different amount of time, there is usually a waiting period despite taking an appointment.
RESPECT THE TIME OF PATIENTS AS WELL. STOP TAKING APPOINTMENT
We are still the old fashioned medical clinic where the condition being treated takes precedence over the ticking clock.

Such is a medical (un) professional this person.
I suggest don’t waste your time and try someone who cares and know how to treat !
